title: JMS: distinguish this project's adapter choices from portable JMS doctrine
summary: The delivered ATM intentionally invokes JMS through reflection/JNDI and creates a non-transacted AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE session for its synchronous request/reply adapter. Those are qualified choices of this boundary, not universal Java/JMS defaults.
invariants: Do not copy the reflection adapter merely because the requested feature is 'JMS'; first inspect the project's declared JMS API/dependency boundary.
Do not infer AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE for a transactional, asynchronous, durable, or redelivery-sensitive consumer from this synchronous request/reply client.
Session/acknowledgement/transaction mode is part of delivery semantics and must be chosen from the actual messaging contract.
correct: Use the typed JMS API when the project deliberately declares and owns that dependency.
Use an adapter/reflection seam only when the project explicitly requires provider/API decoupling of that sort.
Choose acknowledgement/transacted semantics from delivery guarantees, replay/idempotency and failure behavior.
